prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Square premium painterly mythology encyclopedia artwork of UBUME in the specific regional KYUSHU UBUMEDORI BIRD manifestation recorded in Terajima Ryōan's Wakan Sansai Zue (1712), author commentary, translated in Yasui Manami's Japan Review study 2021 pages101-102. That Kyushu account describes a bird resembling a seagull in appearance, voice and size, near the western Japanese sea coast on a dark drizzly night, with phosphorescent ghost-fire where it appears. Show ONE entire gull-like bird standing on a slick dark shoreline rock in light rain. Fully avian head with beak, two folded wings integrated naturally into one feathered body, exactly two bird legs with two feet, one feathered tail. All visible body and tail within frame. White and muted grey plumage, natural yellowish gull beak, wet coastal wind ruffling feathers, no human face or body. A single faint bluish-green phosphorescent flame beside the rock marks its uncanny folkloric presence; this is an environmental supernatural light, not added bird anatomy. Rich detailed mature brushwork, deep forest green coastal shadows, very subtle antique-gold cloud-edge light and mournful eerie night atmosphere. Select only Ryōan's Kyushu gull-like bird form, do NOT combine with the separate Chinese human-breasted bird or usual Japanese maternal human ghost: no human breasts, hands, woman, child, bundles, blood, gore, clothing, horns, extra wings, invented hybrid parts, multiple birds, attacking scene, text, border, signature or watermark.
